facts.text: In 1961, JAARS relocated its headquarters to Waxhaw, North Carolina, after years of service in Latin America.
The 630‑acre JAARS Base began as a 200‑acre donation from the Belk family, expanding over time.
The renovated Cardenas Building, named for former Mexican president Lázaro Cárdenas, now displays JAARS’ founding story and mission work.
A 90‑minute guided tour walks about a mile from the Cardenas Building to the Air, Land and Sea Operations, revealing the base’s history.
Founded in 1948 by William Cameron Townsend, JAARS originally supplied aviation and radio services to Bible translators in remote Latin American regions.
In 1986 JAARS dropped the original acronym meaning, and in 2023 added “Jungle Aviation and Relay Service” to honor its 75‑year heritage.
